text:
sam: Quick sanity check on frontdoor behaviour — when we abort a long-running streaming request (client disconnect / deadline), do we want the proxy to surface the upstream `fallback_reason` header to callers during a fast fallback, or keep it internal? :thinking:

maya: My gut: surface a minimal enum (`fallback=capacity|timeout|degraded`) so product teams can reason about why they got the fallback. don’t leak internal node ids or placement details.

liam: +1 on the enum. also need to decide whether the header is set on the final trailer only or repeated as part of mid-stream control frames for resumable flows. we currently only set trailers.

olga: trailers only is simpler for HTTP/1.1 but nasty for gRPC/HTTP2 streaming where clients care mid-stream. If we expose it mid-stream we need to standardize a control frame with a stable key. ideas: `x-rw-fallback` as a header frame vs a custom gRPC status code extension.

sam: good call. Two policy questions: 1) is the header part of the idempotency contract (i.e., should retries with different fallback reasons be visible to client)? 2) do we allow upstreams to override the fallback enum or do we canonicalize at the gateway?

maya: for (1) treat it as informative only — not part of retry semantics. retries still judged by request idempotency settings. for (2) canonicalize at gateway: map upstream signals to our enum so we don’t have to update SDKs when upstream wording changes.

liam: canonicalization implies we keep a mapping table per model/service. that table needs TTL and a safe default mapping. also, when gateway maps `OOM -> capacity` we should add a small code fragment in the trailer with raw upstream `x-up-reason` for debuggability behind admin-only logging.

olga: agree on admin-only raw reasons. we must avoid accidental PII leaks. add a redaction step to the admin logs pipeline.

sam: implementation sketch:
```yaml
gateway:
  fallback_mapping_ttl: 24h
  fallback_enum: [capacity, timeout, degraded, unknown]
  expose_header: true
  header_name: x-rw-fallback
  admin_raw_header: x-rw-fallback-raw
```

sam: behaviour notes: set `x-rw-fallback` as soon as gateway decides to fall back (so client sees it on a control frame if supported). attach `x-rw-fallback-raw` only to admin logs and to trailers for internal SDKs when `debug=true`.

maya: question: if gateway decides to fall back mid-stream and the client reconnects/resumes, should the resume flow receive the previous `x-rw-fallback` value to indicate prior degradation? might confuse app logic.

liam: prefer not to persist it across resume — the resume should be treated as a fresh call w.r.t signals. but we should emit an event to observability linking session id -> fallback history.

olga: Observability event is good. also, for retries we need to avoid double-counting cost when fallback happens then real model responds. we probably already have billing flags but call it out here.

sam: noted. final compatibility caveats: older SDKs that only expect trailers might miss mid-stream header frames — we'll document a graceful degradation: when control frames unsupported, trailer will include the enum.

infra-bot: deploy plan reminder: this is gated behind `gateway.fallback.header-flag` feature flag. Rolling deploy across edge regions with 1% canary for 12 hours, then 25%, then 100%.

maya: thanks. I'll draft an RFC update summarizing mapping table + admin raw header + observability events.

liam: I'll add tests for gRPC control frame emission and verify no PII in raw logs.

olga: will add redaction step to logging pipeline and a short doc for SDKs. :+1:
